title: Reversing Aging by Refining the Jiaji Gates
author: Zhang Xingchun
excerpt: Always keep this mind, retreating it into the Jiaji aperture, guarding it without ever letting it depart.

inline.s: (The practice of inward-light contemplative healing)
Always keep this mind, retreating it into the Jiaji aperture, guarding it without ever letting it depart.

blocks.text: 1. The Jiaji Aperture — the Qi That Reverses Aging

inline.s: The ancient health practitioners called the method of delaying and reversing aging
the oil-adding, life-prolonging method”
and to add oil one must know the oil-adding aperture, and to prolong life one must know the place where life is prolonged
Where then is this aperture for adding oil and prolonging life? In practice the ancients discovered that the body’s Shanzhong
Tianmu
Niwan
Jiaji
Mingmen
Dantian
and Haidi — these seven key acupoints
are the important points where the body’s primordial qi gathers
Among them, the Jiaji aperture is in turn the key of keys
In the meridian system of traditional Chinese medicine this Jiaji aperture is named
Xinshu (shù
the same as the character ‘shu’ meaning an acupoint)
located one and a half cun on either side of the seventh thoracic vertebra, the gateway through which the heart-qi enters and leaves

And the heart governs the spirit and is the great master of the five viscera and six bowels; hence this single Jiaji point, being bound to all the five viscera and six bowels, is clearly no ordinary point

To verify this, I carried out dozens of inner-refinement experiments in which qi-motion was felt and transmitted, and found that the phenomenon of qi-vibration can occur in any part of the body, yet the vibration issuing from the brain radiates only to the head
The vibration issuing from the qi cavity in the lower dantian radiates only to the belly

Only the vibration issuing from the twin Jiaji gates radiates to every part of the body, above and below, left and right; at the instant of the sudden shudder a vortex of qi is formed within and without the whole body, and the center of this vortex lies precisely within the Jiaji gates

From this it is clear that the sole Jiaji aperture, in linking the two qi of Heaven and man, in seizing the prenatal qi, and in reversing the aging of the human body, holds a role and a significance all its own
The method of practice
chiefly consists in gently closing both eyes and, with inward vision, gazing within at the twin Jiaji points on either side of the seventh thoracic vertebra at the back
The primordial qi and vital essence within and without, above and below the body inevitably converge here, and when the convergence resonates it inevitably gives rise to a co-resonance

Like throwing an electric switch, the whole body suddenly gives a single shudder, and in that great shock the hundred meridians open and close together — this is the very sight of Heaven and man acting in concert
The evidence that the mysterious gate has opened wide

in that instant of the sudden shudder the natural true qi enters the body and transforms oneself — this is the simplest, easiest, most miraculous, most sublime shortcut for seizing the primordial oneness! Practice it thus every day, shudder every night, gather every time, ceaselessly replenishing the depletion of one’s own primal qi with primordial energy — how could one still fear aging quickly?! At this point I have laid bare every secret of the twin Jiaji gates; please do not make light of it, for it is a treasure of an elixir for resisting aging and prolonging life! In particular the elderly should not lose heart: so long as one takes up the practice in time, one can likewise delay and reverse the aging process — hence the old masters say:
As long as a single breath remains, one can restore life
The Ultimate Doctrine of Life and Death
says:
This practice
is of all things the simplest

Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, always keep this mind and retreat it into the Jiaji aperture; then the right qi of Heaven and Earth may be guided in, and together with one’s own primordial true essence it condenses in the dantian to become the root of long life

For by the boundless primordial qi of Heaven and Earth one replenishes one’s own limited body — is this not easy? The student has only to fix upon this aperture and guard it without letting it depart; over long practice it grows
thoroughly familiar
, then within it becomes bright and clear, like the moon resting in water.
That passage above has already set forth the method of inward reflection most clearly, so no further words are needed

blocks.text: 2. The Method of Practice in Three Occasions

inline.s: The pace of life today is fast and competition keen; the great majority of people must study and work under pressure, yet normal cultural, recreational, and social activity cannot be set aside either
How, then, can one truly keep daily work and life from interfering with the practice that reverses aging? In my long practice I have worked out a set of
ordinary
dedicated, and intensive” method combining the three, for whatever it may be worth to readers

First, practice in ordinary time: in the midst of daily work and life, whenever you have a spare moment gently close both eyes and gaze back upon the twin Jiaji gates, turning the consumption of energy into its storing up; to gaze back upon this single aperture is the shortcut

Next, dedicated practice: every night before sleep or every morning before rising, devote from half an hour to a full hour to single-minded practice, persisting until it becomes a habit and an indispensable part of daily life
Fruit and verification
come chiefly from this
Finally, intensive practice: according to one’s own circumstances, set aside a longer stretch of time for concentrated practice
Breakthroughs
rely chiefly on intensive practice
Arranged in this way, none can fail

blocks.text: 3. Silently Guarding the Jiaji Aperture to Enter the Mysterious Gate in an Instant

inline.s: Silently guarding the Jiaji aperture, entering the mysterious gate in an instant
The key to this method lies in the two words
“silent guarding”

Silent guarding is not intentional attending, still less rigid holding; it is quietly and gently letting the mind-spirit retreat into the single Jiaji aperture, as if present and yet absent, as if guarding and yet not guarding
Then of itself the heart-fire is dispersed, the scattered thoughts are dissolved, the agitated mind is stilled, the deluded thoughts are stopped, and one enters the realm of forgetting Heaven
forgetting Earth
and forgetting self

Without one’s knowing when, the whole body is suddenly convulsed, the body trembles and the pulses open, the eyes see golden radiance, the ears hear the sound of thunder, the two kidneys feel as if boiled, and the Jiaji gates swirl like a whirlpool — all manner of effects arise of themselves; and I hold the mind still and unmoving, not a single thought arises, letting them arise and vanish on their own, adding oil in the silence and prolonging life in the transcendence

blocks.text: 4. The Verification of Results in Practice

inline.s: The sights and effects of silently guarding the twin Jiaji gates vary from person to person and with the depth of practice. The most basic and obvious responses may be summed up in the following two phrases of ten characters (“warmth, swelling, motion, shock, swirl — the primordial qi all the more abundant”):

blocks.text: 1. Warmth, Swelling, Motion, Shock, and Swirl

inline.s: Warmth
swelling
writhing motion
vibration
and swirling
are the most basic responses of the Jiaji aperture
and of the whole body
during the practice
Their order is:
First,
one first feels a sense of warmth at the Jiaji point, the warmth growing from small to large;
Second,

thereupon one feels within the warmth a sense of swelling, whose range likewise grows from small to large, at first forming only a ball of qi the size of a table-tennis ball around the Jiaji point, and later gradually expanding until one feels a great ball of qi over the whole chest and back;
Third,

as the practice continues, one again feels qi writhing at the center of this great ball (that is, within the Jiaji point); if at this moment one gazes back within the Jiaji point, a bright speck the size of a grain of rice will form in the brain;
Fourth,
about this same time the whole body, as if an electric shock, suddenly shudders once
; Fifth,
at the same moment as the shudder, one also feels a vortex of qi forming around the Jiaji point as its center, extending above and below and to left and right of the whole body

blocks.text: 2. The Primordial Qi All the More Abundant

inline.s: Particularly abundant primordial qi is the most obvious effect of practicing this art, a powerful proof that its effects appear at once, and the chief criterion for judging whether a session of practice has succeeded
On this point, Master Nan Huaijin, in his book
Meditation and Immortality
has a passage that is both vivid and, I can say, precisely matched to my own experimental experience; I transcribe it below:

“If one can attain a state of total forgetfulness of self, or by the exercise of intelligence set aside all sensation and simply remain in calm non-action waiting for its fullness, it will come, like touching the switch of a motor, with a single click, suddenly releasing into a state where the heart-vision opens wide and the spirit becomes especially full and abundant
Even for those who are ordinarily somewhat stooped, at that moment they will naturally straighten the spine, open the chest, breathe smoothly, and enjoy a wonderfully keen appetite
Quite often, because of this, the spirit becomes over-abundant and sleep does not come easily
For this reason, those who suffer from insomnia would do best to practice in the early morning

In every session, does there occur, in a trance-like state, a sudden shudder of the whole body, and after the shudder a feeling of especially pure and serene joy, as if one had been long asleep and only now awakened? Does the spine straighten of itself, does the whole body feel exceptionally at ease, does the spirit feel exceptionally vigorous? These are the criteria by which the success of each session is judged

With long, sustained practice one generally finds the constitution markedly strengthened, food and sleep markedly reduced, energy abundant, immunity to heat and cold, resistance notably increased, and in the elderly the recovery or strengthening of sexual function
If you do not believe it, try it: it will in any case interfere neither with your everyday work and life nor with your cultural recreation, nor with whatever other practices you follow.

1. For the beginner, the turbid yin-qi of the body is relatively heavy; when true yang arises and fills the whole body, one often feels especially uncomfortable, and so one must persist and persist again, for that sudden full-body shudder often comes precisely in those few seconds of renewed persistence.

2. To obtain a stable health benefit one must practice over the long term; to expect a single effort to last forever is unrealistic. More than ten years ago, a qigong magazine published a treatise on practice by a “long-lived elder,” and because it was so incisive and yet so plain, although I can no longer remember which qigong magazine it was, I remember the elder’s words with perfect clarity. He said: “To refine qi and nurture the spirit is in every case to control them by reversal. So long as the power of this reversal is not lessened, one endures; the moment the power of this reversal is lost, one dies at once. Do not think that once the inner elixir is formed one may do as one pleases.” The meaning is that the process of delaying and reversing aging is like boating against the current: if one does not advance, one falls back. Hence the path of practice must be sustained over the long term, sustained for a lifetime.

blocks.text: Appendix One: The Twin Jiaji Gates Are No Ordinary Aperture

inline.s: Zhang Xingchun

The role and significance of China’s traditional Daoist elixir arts in slowing the aging of the human body and promoting health and longevity are beyond question. The core of the elixir arts is the prenatal oneness of qi (in old texts written with the archaic form, the same as ‘qi’), and this prenatal oneness abides within the single mysterious-gate aperture; hence opening that aperture and seizing the prenatal numinous truth is the key and the shortcut to slowing or even reversing the aging process.
Where, then, is this single mysterious-gate aperture? Zhang Ziyang says:
“This aperture is no common aperture; Heaven and Earth together formed it. It is named the point of spirit and qi, within which lie the essences of Kan and Li.”

In my view, this aperture is the twin Jiaji gates. For the so-called “twin gates” signify the union of Heaven and Earth, of spirit and qi, of Kan and Li. Silently guarding this aperture, Heaven and Earth unite, spirit and qi merge, Kan and Li cross, true yin and true yang cleave to one another, and the prenatal oneness is already present within it. Such a wondrous aperture is by no means comparable to or replaceable by any other gate or aperture, and so it is said, “This aperture is no common aperture.”
Look again at The Ultimate Doctrine of Life and Death:

“The ancient immortals had a saying: The twin Jiaji gates pierce through to the crown of the head; on the road of cultivation this is to be honored above all. It ascends on high to the celestial valley, descends below to the coccyx, and passes through the midst to the heart and kidneys; it summons and gathers the numinous yang and rescues the treasure of life — how is this not the very path of cultivation?”

This shows that the twin Jiaji gates truly hold a special function in cultivation, and are by no means an ordinary gate. The method of practice and its effects the ancient practitioners also set forth very clearly:
“This practice
is of all things the simplest

Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, always keep this mind and retreat it into the Jiaji aperture; then the right qi of Heaven and Earth may be guided in, and with one’s own primordial true essence it condenses in the dantian to become the root of transcendent birth. For by the boundless primordial qi of Heaven and Earth one replenishes one’s own limited body — is this not easy! The student has only to fix upon this aperture and guard it without letting it depart; over long practice it becomes thoroughly familiar, and then within it becomes bright and clear, like the moon resting in water.”
My own practical experience is that the so-called
always keep this mind, retreating it into the Jiaji
aperture

is not a fierce intentional attending to the Jiaji gates, but rather to know them without guarding, to know them without discriminating. For to hold them with deliberate intent is to act in the postnatal mode, which is not only unhelpful but actually harmful. Only to know without guarding, to know without discerning, is to be governed by the prenatal, and only thus can one enter the state as quickly as possible. Whether one can enter the state is the crux of success or failure in practice, because this aperture opens only in a state of dim and distant oblivion — the saying has it that “when opened it becomes an aperture, when closed it becomes a gate.”

Moreover, beginners and those with serious ailments also find it comparatively hard to enter the state, and so before doing so their bodies feel especially uncomfortable; this is the moment when the two qi of right and wrong contend, and at this point one must hold fast, or all previous effort is wasted. And the miracle often arrives within those few minutes, even within a few seconds, of renewed holding. Once the twin Jiaji gates suddenly burst open, one instantly feels the whole body vanish, and a single bright, glittering pearl the size of a grain of millet hangs suspended in the void. This is a priceless treasure and miraculous medicine absolutely without equal in the world — “what the Buddhists call the pearl of muni, what the Daoists call the golden elixir pearl, whereby one may attain long life and immortality.”

blocks.text: A Wondrous Method for Reversing Aging

inline.s: Stand or sit at will, relax the whole body, close the eyes softly, listen quietly to your own breathing, and let the mind-spirit settle.

Then, with inward vision and inward reflection, gaze upon the Jiaji points on either side of the seventh thoracic vertebra, as if present and yet absent, as if guarding and yet not guarding, and quietly, gently let the mind-spirit retreat into the aperture, entering the realm of forgetting things and forgetting self. After a time a sense of warmth arises, the warmth growing from small to large; then a sense of swelling appears, its range likewise growing from small to large, until a lump of qi forms and gradually expands, and one can feel qi writhing within.

If at this point one can be without a single thought and wholly non-active, the whole body suddenly shudders, as if an electric shock, and in that shudder the hundred meridians open and close together; Heaven and man act in concert, the prenatal oneness transforms one’s own body, and without one’s knowledge the primordial energy is gathered to replenish the primordial qi already depleted within oneself.

After the practice the heart-vision opens wide and the spirit is exceptionally vigorous — the obvious proof of abundant primordial qi and the powerful evidence of the method’s instant efficacy. Practicing thus every day, shudders every day, gathering every day, adding oil in the silence and prolonging life in the undifferentiated whole, the sexual desire that had already dried up revives. As my maternal grandfather recounted this, his joy overflowed; he said with deep feeling that the arising of true yang is where the reversal of aging begins, that it must be treasured and not squandered, and that one must persist in practice over the long term before one can return to the state of childhood.
The old masters have a saying:
“As long as a single breath remains, one can restore life.”
The elderly should not, thinking themselves already old, lose heart; they should take up the practice in good time.
If middle-aged people and those of weak constitution can practice this method, beyond dispelling illness and strengthening the body, they will all the more delay the aging process.

If one is busy at work, then whenever there is a spare moment just close the eyes softly and gaze back upon the twin Jiaji gates, turning the consumption of energy into its storing up — that too counts as a method of strengthening the body.

If one can set aside half an hour to a full hour each day for devoted practice and persist over the long term, it will surely make the constitution markedly stronger, reduce food and sleep, render one immune to heat and cold, and markedly raise one’s resistance.
This method is simple and easy, and does not interfere with the practice of other arts; anyone interested may try it and see for themselves.

blocks.text: Appendix Two: The Twin Jiaji Gates

inline.s: Tian Guanglin
The ancients say:
“The twin Jiaji gates pierce through to the crown of the head; on the path of cultivation this is to be honored above all.”

This is not only the shortcut of the immortal arts, but also the proper method of mending deficiencies and prolonging life by adding oil. Gathering the spirit at the Jiaji gates has the power to cleanse the heart and still the thoughts, and can lead one into the state of no-mind and self-forgetting. Thereupon it penetrates the Niwan (
Baihui

), and descends by the Mingmen to join the primal ancestral qi, fusing essence, qi, and spirit into one, so as to nourish the root-source and rescue the treasure of life. Hence it is the foundational practice of the Daoist cultivation of both nature and life. Attending with the mind upon the twin Jiaji gates, above it reaches the celestial valley and the Niwan, below it reaches the Yinqiao (
Huiyin
and
the coccyx, and by the central yellow passage it radiates straight through, causing the true qi to circulate through the whole body and open all the hundred meridians.
[Niwan] The crown of the head
— the Niwan palace
, also called the celestial valley
, which is the Baihui point.

blocks.text: 1. The Central Yellow Opening Straight Through — Cultivating Both Nature and Life

inline.s: The twin Jiaji gates lie at the exact center, above and below, of the twenty-four vertebrae of the spine (that is, the hollow aperture midway between the tips of the two shoulder blades at the back). Min Yide said of this aperture:

“Behind the spine and in front of the stomach, at once formed and yet unformed. Before it opens it is called the mysterious gate; after it opens it is called the mysterious aperture. When the student reaches the utmost of emptiness and the height of stillness, this aperture appears. Embryonic breathing takes its rest here. The primordial spirit within my body rises and descends here; this is what is called the road of attaining the Way.”

The Huangji Hebi Immortal Scripture says this very place is the central yellow, also named the chamber of spirit and the yellow chamber — its names are many, but in short it is the resting place of the prenatal nature, rising and descending through the center, and for that reason it is called the central yellow radiating straight through. Here is the shortcut to realizing the Way, the road of the prenatal ascent and descent. Hence it is the place where the embryo is formed, nurtured, and brought forth. The Changes says:
“The yellow center pervades all principle; the right position dwells in the body; beauty resides within it, and harmony is its utmost.”
Therefore when one gathers the spirit at the Jiaji gates and feels it flow with utter smoothness, with a burning heat like fire, this is the verification of having entered the aperture.

The practitioner has only, in walking, standing, sitting, and lying down, always to keep this mind hidden in the Jiaji aperture, guarding it without letting it depart; then the right qi of Heaven and Earth, following the breath of the nose, is guided in, and of itself condenses with one’s own primordial true essence in the dantian, becoming the treasure of one’s life-nurturing. Over long practice it becomes thoroughly familiar, and within it grows bright and clear, like the moon in water. Naturally one’s perverse fire is scattered, one’s scattered thoughts dissolved, one’s agitated mind stilled, one’s deluded thoughts stopped. The deluded thoughts ceasing, the true breath appears of itself. The true breath is breathless, the true thought is thoughtless. The breath ceasing, the root of life is forever firm; the thought ceasing, the nature-body forever abides. Nature abiding and life firm, breath and thought both vanished, one enters the realm of emptiness — this is the first step in cultivating both nature and life.

blocks.text: 2. Gathering the Spirit in the Qi Aperture to Rescue the Treasure of Life

inline.s: The twin Jiaji gates are the path of cultivation. For this aperture can ascend to the celestial valley (
Baihui

), descend to the coccyx, pass through the midst to the heart and kidneys, summon and gather the numinous yang, and rescue the treasure of life. Is this not the path of cultivation? Yet to open this aperture one must first visualize the root of the mountain (
the point between the eyebrows

), and enter the realm of emptiness; only then does the breath of respiration gradually pass through the Niwan, open the Jiaji gates, reach the ancestral aperture of the heavenly mind, and join the primal ancestral qi. Nanqiao Zi says: The marvel of this practice

“lies in moving the spirit gathered at the twin gates to be hidden in the qi aperture, guarding it without letting it depart; then the primal ancestral qi of Heaven and Earth can be linked through and enter.”
The Huangji Hebi Immortal Scripture says:

“In this practice, once the spirit has entered the aperture, the respiration is wholly within the aperture, and the breathing of my nose is but a single point, so faint as to be almost absent — only this is the verification of having entered the aperture. Verifying again and again without fail, one attains the true gold.”

blocks.text: 3. The Proper Method of Repairing Deficiencies and Prolonging Life by Adding Oil

inline.s: Each day, when the practitioner enters the chamber to practice, he must first loosen his clothes and unfasten his belt, put down all ten thousand attachments, then exhale one or two breaths of turbid air, and slowly inhale the pure qi of the world outside into the Jianggong (
the middle dantian

). Once the mind is calm and the breath even, he uses the intent to make both eyes look level ahead, and then brings the two lights to converge into one. In this way he places the thought upon the point between the eyebrows, the root of the mountain, and fixes it there for a long time. Then by intent he raises it to the Niwan (
Baihui

). Again he turns it back through the jade pillow and pours it straight into the Jiaji gates. Once the spirit has reached the Jiaji gates, he should quiet the heart and still the breath, nurture his vast and noble qi, attend to nothing else, be single in this alone, and not let a thought arise and scatter elsewhere.
[Jianggong, pronounced jiàng]
That is, the middle dantian.
The Immortal Scripture says: “The Jianggong is the middle dantian, the dwelling of stored qi.” The Secrets of Cultivating the Real says: “The heart is the Jianggong and the middle dantian.”

Practicing thus one or two hours each day, or sitting all the more, is better. For those of strong qi it takes five or six days, for those of weak qi ten days or half a month, before one feels the Jiaji gates hot as blazing fire, and there is a sense of throbbing. Only after this manifestation appears does the practitioner, with his intent, send this blazing heat into the hollow aperture between the two kidneys. Then he will feel both flanks of the waist also throbbing like a turning pulley; and observing that the throbbing will not cease, he sends it with intent into the Yinqiao (
Huiyin

). Once it has reached the Yinqiao he again feels it quivering and throbbing; though it throbs he pays it no heed, and after a long time he feels the whole body at ease, the heart as if drunk with bliss, all the channels of the body seeming alive, warm and glowing as if sitting in a spring breeze, resting deeply at the Yinqiao and the sea-floor.
[Yinqiao] The Yinqiao point holds an important place on the meridians. It lies between the two yin parts, called by Chinese medicine the Huiyin point,
and by the yogic school the “root wheel”

After a short while, naturally the quivering settles and the throbbing stops. Carefully observe the true-yang qi produced at the Yinqiao, rising like smoke from a stove, ascending to the lower belly and then to the navel wheel; after a time it again descends from the navel wheel to the Yinqiao, ascending and descending thus, using stillness to guide the naturally transforming mechanism. At this time one must only guard against the rising of a thought; if a thought arises it scatters, and though one sits it is of no avail. In short, in practicing this method one must keep this numinous, undimmed spirit dwelling forever in the Yinqiao without going out. Once it has dwelt long in peace, the spirit naturally transforms into qi, and qi naturally transforms into essence. The essence being sufficient, qi is produced of itself, and the spirit flourishes of itself; essence, qi, and spirit become a single undifferentiated whole — and this is to attain the goal.

blocks.text: Appendix Three: Pointing to the Mystery of the Jiaji Gate

inline.s: Liu Li
Mr. Wang Ziqiang’s
Uncovering the Secrets of the Jiaji Gate

, in that article, based on his own experience in practice, offers a preliminary account of the wondrous efficacy of the Jiaji gate in curing illness and nurturing life. After reading it I was deeply moved by Mr. Wang’s spirit of daring to practice
and daring to explore.

But since the article was, after all, an exploratory piece occasioned by a “chance encounter,” it did not yet set forth in full the concrete role of the Jiaji gate in cultivation or the correct method of practice. Now, following my teacher’s transmission and the Daoist elixir classics,
I will set the secrets of the Jiaji gate completely before you, for the benefit of the reader.

The Jiaji gate, also called the pulley gate, lies at the very center of the twenty-four segments of the spine, corresponding front and back to the “Zhongwan point” of Chinese acupuncture. It ascends to the Baihui, descends clear to the coccyx, passes through the midst to the heart, and externally can gather the numinous yang qi of Heaven and Earth while internally rescuing the treasure on which the whole life depends.

[The three gates of the back] Behind the head is the jade-pillow gate, at the Jiaji is the pulley gate, and at the juncture of water and fire is the coccyx gate. [Pulley (lù lu)] A device set over a well for drawing up the bucket on a rope.
Always Turn the Winch of Life

Practicing at this place, the immortal classics call it the “oil-adding, life-prolonging method” and the “method of arresting the breath”; for dispelling illness, strengthening the body, and even awakening latent powers it has an instant and wondrous efficacy. It is a great method kept secret and never passed on lightly in the immortal arts, and it runs through the
entire course
of the Daoist elixir practice.
As The Ultimate Doctrine of Life and Death says:

“This method cannot be left aside from beginning to end. At the outset it has the merit of rescuing, repairing, protecting, and aiding; in the second stage the merit of turning the flowing to oneself; in the third stage the merit of adding oil and prolonging life; in the fourth stage the merit of helping the fire and carrying the gold; in the fifth stage the merit of the fire’s mutual fulfillment; in the sixth stage, the embryo formed, the merit of bathing; and in the seventh stage, the merit of warming and nourishing, of suckling the infant
The infant emerges from the sea of suffering; when the shore is reached no boat is needed, and only then is this practice of no further use.”

Hence it has always been treasured by cultivators of the real from antiquity; those who know it never lightly show it to others, holding that “it cannot be transmitted to any but the greatly virtuous and greatly accomplished.” Its beneficial effects are extremely many, and it enjoys the fine reputation that “once the Jiaji gates open, a hundred diseases do not arise.” As to its chief points, they number about four great effects:

blocks.text: One: Gather the Primordial Spirit and Dissipate the Cognition-Spirit

inline.s: Primordial spirit and cognition-spirit are terms from the ancient Daoist elixir practice. The cognition-spirit refers to the miscellaneously deluded mind of a person contaminated by the seven emotions and six desires of the postnatal life, while the primordial spirit refers to the original, pure, spontaneous mind, like the state of an infant who knows nothing and discriminates nothing, all innocence and no impurity. The first task of our practice is to sweep away the seven emotions and six desires, thereby eliminating the interference of the cognition-spirit with the body, and to let the primordial spirit take charge and govern, for only thus can the power of practice ceaselessly rise and at last reach the ideal state of great ease of body and mind.

But at present most practitioners use the cognition-spirit in charge, that is, they practice with personal emotions such as joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. Even if the primordial spirit appears for a moment and one sees a sudden light, one immediately gives rise to a mind of delight and a feeling of attachment, and the primordial spirit is again drowned by the cognition-spirit. To gather the primordial spirit is in truth a difficult matter, and its shortcut is to attend with the mind upon the Jiaji gates. My teacher’s Secret Transmission of the Heavenly Primordium says:
“The student has only to
fix upon

this aperture, guarding it without letting it depart; over long practice it becomes thoroughly familiar, and then within it becomes bright and clear, like the moon resting in water. Naturally one disperses the perverse fire, dissolves the scattered delusions, stills the striving mind, and stops the deluded thoughts. The deluded thoughts ceasing, the primordial spirit becomes vast, and the practice has its lord.”

blocks.text: Two: Bring about Embryonic Breathing and Transform the Ordinary Breathing

inline.s: The term embryonic breathing is no doubt familiar to everyone; it is
the name given to

that state in which the practitioner, in deep meditative stillness, breathes so subtly that neither he himself nor anyone about him can detect any movement of breath through nose and mouth. One who reaches this condition has every illness dispelled, is brimming with vitality, and feels as though his very body and mind have been entirely transformed, a qualitative leap upon the path of cultivation and the very goal for which every practitioner yearns.
The Immortal Scripture of Master Yin, Orthodox Lineage of the Eastern Flower, Imperial Pole, Opening and Closing, on Attaining the Way, says:
"By intently and earnestly focusing the mind on the paired gate of the Jiaji region, one naturally opens the single aperture of the Heavenly Heart
(Author's note: Heavenly Heart here refers to the spot one cun and three fen within the navel, where prenatal primal qi and primal yang gather together.)

. There one connects with the primordial ancestral qi of prenatal Heaven, and as a lodestone draws iron, so kindred natures draw near; this is what the True Man Zhuangzi meant by 'the breath of the true person reaches to the heels.'

Practiced long enough, each inhalation and exhalation enters the qi cavity, a wonder that arises of itself. In time the embryonic breath settles, the yin'e takes form, and the road to long life lies open."

This passage plainly instructs that by merely focusing the mind on the Jiaji region one can draw the primordial mixed qi of Heaven and Earth into the dantian, and in time naturally accomplish embryonic breathing.

[Yin'e] The Zhouyi Cantong Qi says: 'Nourish the yin'e with mindful tending, gather the spirit to perfect the body.' Zhu Yuanyu of the Qing dynasty annotates: 'The yin'e is none other than the primal spirit.'

Yet most of those in the qigong world who practice embryonic breathing have misread the meaning of the ancients' line 'of old the holy teacher passed on his oral formula, only gather the spirit into the qi cavity.' They take the busy, calculating conscious mind and use it to concentrate directly on the lower dantian, and then add regulated breathing, counting the breath, and holding the breath, hoping thereby to succeed. Not only do they fail of their wish, but a host of ill effects arise, exactly as Mr. Nan Huaijin thrice sharply rebukes: 'Men readily suffer seminal emission, and women are prone to flooding and spotting.'
My teacher has said:
In regulating breath one must regulate the true breath; in refining spirit one must refine the unrefined spirit.

The true breath is embryonic breathing; the unrefined spirit is the primal spirit. Both gathering the spirit and regulating the breath have their oral formulas; without them one fears the thinking consciousness will wrongly couple with the breath and congeal a phantom elixir, which harms the practitioner instead.
gather the spirit into the qi cavity

means that one must await the manifestation of the primal spirit and then gather it, bringing it down into the dantian, before true embryonic breathing is accomplished. The student should first hold to the Jiaji region so as to condense the primal spirit; when the merit is fully matured, then carry the spirit condensed there into the dantian and keep it there, and he will of himself attain the wondrous state of embryonic breathing. This is the right path of cultivation."

blocks.text: Third: the marvelous function of opening the barriers and unfolding the apertures

inline.s: To open the Greater and Lesser Orbital Cycles is a very popular topic in the qigong world today and the goal that the vast majority of practitioners pursue. But the orbital cycle methods now in vogue are for the most part the mind-led cycle and the meridian cycle. The former guides the inner sensation of qi by mind along the Conception and Governing vessels or the twelve regular meridians; for moving the blood and qi and inducing stillness it certainly has its effects
yet in truth it is only a stream of consciousness

The latter is the true qi circulating of itself along the meridians, needing no guidance of the mind, and its effects are excellent; but the route it travels is confined to the space between muscle and sinew, lacking depth and breadth, and so it too is not the true orbital cycle.

The so-called orbital cycle means that the true qi circulates unimpeded through the four limbs and hundred bones, the five organs and six viscera, down even to the eighty-four thousand pores of the whole body, the vast vital breath overflowing the four members. My teacher says in the Secret Transmission of Heavenly Origin:

"The method of opening the barriers lies wondrously in keeping the spirit on the single aperture of the paired gate. This aperture can connect the twelve meridians, can thread the eighty-four thousand pores, and pierce through the hundred joints of the limbs and the five organs and six viscera. When the spirit is condensed here and one practices holding the breath, in time the essence fills and the qi transforms, and this transformation of itself bursts open the three barriers, flows through the hundred channels, spreads freely into the four limbs, and every aperture becomes radiant. The Book of Changes says,
the yellow center penetrates and orders all, and the proper position abides in the body

, which is precisely what this means. At this point one has the verification of holding the breath until qi issues from each of the eighty-four thousand pores; this is for those of superior faculties and keen capacity. As for those of middling or lower capacity, or those whose practice is slack and slow, the barriers and apertures are hard to open; one must wait until the fire blazes in the dantian and the two kidneys seethe as if boiled, then practice according to the method, and only then can they be opened."

blocks.text: Fourth: the marvelous effect of replenishing the essential qi and restoring the youthful body

inline.s: Because of marriage and child-rearing and the toil of worldly affairs, by middle age a person has consumed the greater part of his essential qi, and often shows such symptoms as yin deficiency with blazing fire, shortness of breath and weariness of spirit. If one wishes to bring his qigong practice to a higher plane soon, the urgent need is to replenish the essential qi and return to the vigorous, flourishing health of youth.

As for the methods of replenishing essential qi, there are the tonic of medicine, the tonic of food, and the tonic of qi, that is, the method of qigong cultivation. But the first two demand a high level of medical knowledge before one may use them; otherwise an indiscriminate tonic leads only to dire consequence. How often one sees people recklessly take hot tonics such as ginseng and deer antler, and gorge themselves on chicken, duck, fish, and meat, calling it the fine art of nourishment. Little do they know that misapplied heating medicines only inflame the heart-fire, so that yin and yang fall out of balance and one suffers bleeding from nose and mouth and an unbearable agitation; and that an excess of rich food thickens the blood and qi, so that one falls prey to wasting-thirst, that is diabetes, and such intractable complaints as blockage of the heart and cerebral vessels. These disorders have already become the common diseases of our day, which people call the illnesses of affluence, and this truly deserves attention.

The ancients said, 'The tonic of medicine is not equal to the tonic of food, and the tonic of food is not equal to the tonic of qi,' and so it truly is. When the student, in holding to the Jiaji region, has reached a certain stage of merit, with its attendant marks of verification, and then practices further with the 'method of adding oil to restore the life force' (in truth the 'method of filling the essence and replenishing the marrow'), within a hundred days he can replenish the essential qi consumed over half a lifetime, and so radiate youth and grow fair again. My teacher says in the Secret Transmission of Heavenly Origin:

"In the womb the infant's Jiaji region is naturally open. Later, when the term is complete and birth takes place, the seven apertures abruptly open, and the qi, the vessels, the spirit, and the light no longer rise and fall by this passage, so that the blood grows foul and, gathering by degrees, gradually stagnates and congeals. Who would know that this very spot is the old road by which I first came into the world? If this aperture can be opened, no illness remains. A scholar who dwells in the world for decades, wearied by fame and profit and busied with affairs, never sparing his toil, gathers many ailments. If he can but know the secret of producing fire and kindling yang here, then whether old or young, his kidney-yang turns from weak to strong as easily as turning over the hand."

Of the manifold great functions of the Jiaji pass in cultivation I have set out above four in brief. As for the others, such as moistening the five viscera, benefiting the qi and nourishing the yin, replenishing the blood and calming the spirit, the student can truly experience them in the course of actual practice, so I will not belabor them. I hope this essay may awaken wide recognition among practitioners of the importance of the Jiaji pass, and that they then earnestly begin from the foundation of strengthening body and mind; only when the pure qian body is restored should they pursue the higher powers. Otherwise, to speak of 'the five eyes and the six supernormal faculties' while wearing a sickly countenance is no different from a madman's empty talk of dreams. And even if one gains a little, it is most unstable, or is but the morbid reflection of an imbalance of yin and yang in the body.
Finally,
let us
draw the whole essay together with the poem of Langranzi recorded in the ancient elixir scriptures:
The paired gates at the spine pierce through the crown; / of every path of practice this one holds the renown.
Swallow ever the Flower Pool's water bright; / the Primal Lord of the Purple Court soars to the height.
Let qi ever fill and the joints be opened through; / then the essence is full and the Valley Spirit holds true.
When shall you learn the deathless road, and how? / Be grateful to the one who first taught you till now.
